neighbours.label: the small-amount hedge: ' bit' in 'a bit' / 'a bit of', ' little' in 'a little' before an adjective or comparative, and ' least' in 'at least in part'; strong degree words and literal bits or sizes stay low
fire: The first chapter can feel a little confusing to new readers.
Prices this spring were a little higher than last year.
With a bit of patience, the seedlings will recover.
Our hotel had a bit of a noise problem at night.
The decline may be explained, at least in part, by the drought.
She sounded a little annoyed on the phone this morning.
He needed a bit of luck to pass the exam.
The new model is a little faster but costs more.
quiet: The first chapter can feel very confusing to new readers.
Prices this spring were far higher than last year.
With enough patience, the seedlings will recover.
Our hotel had a serious noise problem at night.
The decline may be explained, almost entirely, by the drought.
She sounded quite annoyed on the phone this morning.
He needed some luck to pass the exam.
The dentist replaced the worn drill bit before the next patient.
